notes: KNOWN FAILING (partially) — muse genuinely detaches a slow bash command (tool_batch.effect.terminal.outcome.task_completion.kind=="pending"). Commit 10e0c6554 fixed the muse parser (core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/parser.go: parseToolBatchEffectTerminal / parseInboxItemQueued) so BackgroundProcessCount now genuinely goes non-zero on spawn and clears on the task's own termination notification — confirmed via live replay of 3 real transcripts (2 organic corpus records + 1 freshly recorded with this exact recipe via `muse exec`), see metadata.json's assessment body. But the classifier's working->ready gate (session.SessionMetrics.IsAgentDone(), core/domain/session/metrics.go) only consults HasLiveBackgroundProcess, which requires a registered liveness PROBE (lsof output-path or PID kill-0, core/application/services/session_detector_activity.go:hasBackgroundProbe) — muse's task_id satisfies neither, so the session is still expected to go ready prematurely while BackgroundProcessCount>0. RECIPE: the prompt runs `sleep 45 && echo BG_DONE` and replies the literal token BGPROC_OK IMMEDIATELY once the tool call returns control, without polling. Live-measured with this exact recipe (sleep=20 variant): premature working->ready at +27.46s from turn_start while BackgroundProcessCount was still 1, real drain (agent_continuation, BackgroundProcessCount->0) at +29.81s, true final ready at +45.23s — the recipe's sleep was lengthened to 45s (pushing genuine resolution to an estimated ~55s, not independently re-measured at this longer duration) specifically so bg_alive_working's duration_at_least_ms window (35000ms, raised from a vacuous-pass 12000ms that the live probe showed was too short to even observe the failure) falls inside the gap between the premature-ready timing (~27s, driven by muse's own foreground-wait ceiling + model latency, roughly independent of total sleep length) and the new genuine resolution (~55s, driven by sleep length). CORRECT arc per the scenario spec: ready->working, held working through the full background lifetime, then a single working->ready — EXPECTED to fail today at the premature-ready point. Single-birth session model (muse's session id = directory basename, fixed at session start): session_birth anchors to "start" unpinned; every later phase is pinned same_session_as:session_birth because muse spawns companion reminder/goal-check subagents freely (also tagged execution_mode:"background") that could otherwise satisfy an unpinned phase vacuously. No cost is ever persisted for either muse-spark-1.2 or muse-spark-1.3-contributor (no pricing/alias entry), so cost_nonzero is false; tokens are used on every model call, so tokens_nonzero is true. model corrected to muse-spark-1.2, the value actually observed on this machine's most recent live sessions (both an organic corpus recording and this assessment's own live probe), replacing an older sample's muse-spark-1.3-contributor.

text: Session appears in ready shortly after the muse TUI finishes launching (--trust-workspace skips the first-run trust dialog)
muse-bin PID bound to the real session via its .session.lock held flock fd
User prompt drives ready -> working (run.started -> EventType=user_message) on the same session that was born ready

While the detached bash process (sleep 45) is alive, the session must stay working — it must NOT settle to ready once the model replies BGPROC_OK and the tool call itself returns. CONFIRMED FAILING (not an open question): a live probe using this exact recipe (sleep=20 variant) measured the daemon going working->ready at +27.46s from turn_start while BackgroundProcessCount was still 1 — the classifier's ready gate (IsAgentDone/HasLiveBackgroundProcess) does not consult BackgroundProcessCount and muse has no liveness probe (no PID/output-path in the raw record) to set HasLiveBackgroundProcess instead. duration_at_least_ms is set to 35000 (inside the gap between the ~27s premature-ready and the ~55s genuine resolution this longer sleep creates) specifically so this phase's window reaches far enough to observe the failure — the original 12000ms floor was a vacuous pass that would not have caught it.

After the background process exits (the task's own kind:"task" terminal event fires and its result drains from the inbox), the session settles working -> ready exactly once on the same session max_delay_ms raised to 90000 (from 60000) to comfortably exceed the ~70s true-final-ready projected for the sleep=45 recipe (linear-scaled from a measured +45.23s at sleep=20; record should confirm).
